svg.text: Graph Coloring — Chromatic Number & Greedy Algorithms
Problem Definition & Chromatic Number
• k-coloring: assign one of k colors to each vertex
so no two adjacent vertices share a color
• χ(G) = chromatic number = minimum k for valid coloring
• χ(G) = 1 iff G has no edges (empty graph)
• χ(G) = 2 iff G is bipartite (2-colorable)
• χ(complete graph Kₙ) = n (every vertex needs unique color)
• Computing χ(G) exactly is NP-hard for general graphs
Greedy Coloring & Welsh-Powell
• Greedy: for each vertex (in some order), assign lowest color
not used by any neighbor → O(V + E)
• Result ≤ Δ(G) + 1 colors (Δ = max degree) — often optimal
• Welsh-Powell: sort vertices by degree descending, then greedy
→ better color count in practice, same O(V log V + E) complexity
• DSatur: choose vertex with most distinct neighbor colors next
→ finds χ(G) exactly for many practical graph classes
Special Graph Classes
• Bipartite graphs: χ = 2, detect via BFS 2-coloring O(V+E)
• Planar graphs: χ ≤ 4 (Four Color Theorem, 1976)
• Interval graphs: χ = clique number ω(G), greedy on endpoint order
• Chordal graphs: perfect graphs — greedy on perfect elimination order
• Cycle graphs: χ = 2 (even cycle) or χ = 3 (odd cycle)
• Trees: always χ = 2 (bipartite), greedy BFS coloring works
• Brook's theorem: χ(G) ≤ Δ(G) unless G is Kₙ or odd cycle
Applications
• Register allocation: variables = vertices, conflicts = edges
colors = registers → k-coloring with k = # physical registers
• Exam scheduling: courses = vertices, shared students = edges
colors = time slots → minimize exam periods (χ time slots)
• Map coloring: regions = vertices, borders = edges (χ ≤ 4)
• Frequency assignment: transmitters = vertices, interference = edges
• Task scheduling with conflicts: parallel execution with constraints
• Sudoku: graph coloring on a 81-vertex conflict graph (9 colors)
Exact χ(G): NP-hard in general
Greedy: O(V+E), uses ≤ Δ+1 colors
Bipartite check: O(V+E) via BFS
Planar graphs: χ ≤ 4 (Four Color Thm)
Key app: register allocation
